title: Buy Now, Pay Later: The Math on 4 Payments

lines.say: Buy now, pay later. Four easy payments. Zero interest.
Used carefully, it really can cost nothing. But it's built to make spending feel smaller than it is. Let's run the numbers.

lines.cap: Here's how it works. A $400 purchase becomes four payments of $100, every two weeks. Pay on time, and pay-in-4 plans often cost zero interest.
lines.say: Here's how it works. A four hundred dollar purchase becomes four payments of a hundred, every two weeks. Pay on time, and pay-in-four plans often cost zero interest.
So where's the catch? Three places.
Catch one. Stacking.
One plan is easy to track. But they add up quietly.
Sneakers, one twenty.
Headphones, two hundred.
A grocery run, one sixty.
And a gift, two eighty.

scene.label: Due every two weeks
scene.sub: almost double the $100 of fun money in our example budget

lines.cap: $760 in total, split into fours. That's $190 due every two weeks.
lines.say: Seven sixty in total, split into fours. That's a hundred ninety due every two weeks.
In our example budget, fun money is a hundred per paycheck. These payments alone take almost double.
Catch two. Fees when a payment misses.

lines.cap: If autopay hits an empty account, you can get a late fee from the lender and an overdraft fee from your bank. Say $8, plus $35.
lines.say: If autopay hits an empty account, you can get a late fee from the lender, and an overdraft fee from your bank. Say eight dollars, plus thirty-five.

lines.cap: $43 in fees on a $100 payment. Fees vary, so check your own lender and bank.
lines.say: Forty-three dollars in fees, on a hundred dollar payment. Fees vary, so check your own lender and bank.
Catch three. It makes things feel cheaper.

lines.cap: $100 sounds like a lot less than $400. That's the point. And some longer buy-now-pay-later loans do charge interest, so read which kind you're getting.
lines.say: A hundred dollars sounds like a lot less than four hundred. That's the point. And some longer buy-now-pay-later loans do charge interest, so read which kind you're getting.

scene.head: USE IT ONLY IF…
items: You could pay in full today
Payments fit inside your fun money
Autopay comes from a funded account

lines.say: So here's a simple rule.
Only use it if you could pay in full today.
If the payments fit inside your fun money.
If it's your only active plan.
And if autopay comes from an account that's funded.
